You'll work in scorekit, a small library that scores model answers against reference answers.
Everything on screen comes from four replay scripts.
Here's what you'll walk away with.

slides.body: In one sentence: 🟢 SAFE, git log walks the graph from the tips you name, filters the commits it meets, and prints each survivor in the format you choose.
Precisely, think in four stages, and place every option in one of them.

slides.direction: The four-stage table from section 14A.9.
slides.caption: Stage two is the filter: which of the visited commits are shown.

slides.direction: The four-stage table from section 14A.9.
slides.caption: Stage three is the order: --date-order, --topo-order, --author-date-order, --reverse.

slides.direction: The four-stage table from section 14A.9.
slides.caption: Stage four is the print: --oneline, --format, --graph, --decorate, --stat, -p, --name-status.

slides.direction: The root-cause box of section 14A.9, one line at a time.
slides.text:
Observed behavior : --since=2026-09-10 --until=2026-09-11 omits four commits made on the morning of the 10th
                    and includes one made on the morning of the 11th
Git state         : nothing unusual; the commits exist and carry those dates
Mechanism         : Git's date parser took the time of day, which the argument left out, from the clock
Root cause        : "2026-09-10" was read as "10 September at the present time of day", here 12:51
Why Git does this : the same parser serves "yesterday" and "2 days ago", which are meant relative to now;
                    the manual notes only that "today" means the last midnight
Correct fix       : write the time: --since='2026-09-10 00:00' --until='2026-09-11 00:00'
Prevention        : in scripts and incident notes always give a full timestamp, and state the time zone

items: A date filter that drops the morning. Root cause: a date without a time takes the present time of day from the clock, so --since=2026-09-10 meant the tenth at 12:51.

"It was committed on Tuesday, why does the filter not find it?" Root cause: --since and --until compare the committer date, and a cherry-pick or rebase gives a commit a new committer date while keeping the author date.
A search that misses commits on other branches. Root cause: without --all the walk starts at HEAD; the filter never saw the commits.

git log -- path omits a change you know was made. Root cause: with merges in the history the default path mode prunes side branches that did not contribute to the final content; --full-history disables the pruning.
A CI job whose git shortlog prints nothing. Root cause: with no revision and a standard input that is not a terminal, shortlog reads a log from standard input.
